elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 gives Customer exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer; the definition of Deliverable includes specified reports, materials, and other customer-specific work product.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 provides that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, which is defined to include Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Sections 14.3 and 13.2 apply an express perpetual licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable embedded Vendor Technology licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and grants Vendor only a limited processing right for specified service-related purposes.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument. No such instrument is present in the supplied language.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains Vendor Technology under Section 14.3, while the Deliverable definition excludes Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead gives Customer outright ownership through an assignment with no term limit, which is broader than a perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment of all right, title, and interest contains no revocation or termination right and provides a stronger right than an irrevocable licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Customer receives all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable without territorial limitation; embedded Vendor Technology is also expressly licensed worldwide under Section 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Customer owns the Deliverables without any use-based royalty, and the licence covering embedded Vendor Technology is expressly royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's unrestricted ownership of all rights in each Deliverable permits business use and modification; Section 13.2 also expressly permits use, modification, and derivative works for embedded Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As owner of all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable, Customer may grant downstream licences for its business, a broader authority than a sublicense right.
